definition: In probability theory and related fields, the life-time of correlation measures the timespan over which there is appreciable autocorrelation or cross-correlation in stochastic processes..
details: In probability theory and related fields, the life-time of correlation measures the timespan over which there is appreciable autocorrelation or cross-correlation in stochastic processes.

explainer.lead: The life-time of correlation is the timespan over which there is appreciable autocorrelation or cross-correlation in stochastic processes. It matters for knowing how long past observations remain informative about the present.

tiers.eli5: How long a signal keeps remembering its own past before it goes back to being unrelated.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to set window lengths and sampling intervals so that data captures the correlation structure. A pitfall is assuming a single lifetime when the process decays at different rates across scales.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined in probability theory as the timespan over which appreciable autocorrelation or cross-correlation persists in stochastic processes. No formula or formal bound is specified.

explainer.example: If a process's correlation decays to near zero within a short span, that span is its life-time of correlation.
